description: parse_mf7_at_temperature selects the nearest tabulated temperature's S(a,b) tables. For a requested temperature between tabulated points, interpolate S(a,b) across temperature (NJOY interpolates). Currently snaps to nearest; report via selected_temperature(). Low priority - target temps (293.6K) are tabulated exactly. From op-cjw.19.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
RE-PRIORITISATION CANDIDATE (audit 2026-08-11, from op-hc2o). This bead is P4 on the stated rationale 'target temps (293.6K) are tabulated exactly'. That rationale does not hold for HTR-10.

The IAEA HTR-10 B1-B4 benchmarks are specified at 20/120/250 C = 293.15/393.15/523.15 K. The ENDF/B-VIII.0 graphite evaluations tabulate S(alpha,beta) at 296, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 1000, 1200, 1600, 2000 K (verified by parsing tsl-crystalline-graphite.endf MAT=30 with this port). Nearest-tabulated selection therefore snaps 393.15 K -> 400 K and 523.15 K -> 500 K, the latter a 23 K error, and hot operation lands between the widening 600/700/800/1000 K points.

Distinct from op-1y4y, which is the COHERENT-ELASTIC temperature defect (extra-temperature S(E) tables discarded entirely). This bead is the INELASTIC S(alpha,beta) interpolation.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content: ADDRESSED for both channels 2026-08-11 (this session; not committed yet). Chose INTERPOLATION, not refusal, inside the tabulated range: S(alpha,beta) (and coherent S(E)) are interpolated point-by-point between the two bracketing tabulated temperatures using the LI law the evaluation specifies (graphite MT4: LI=4, log-lin in T; MT2: LI=2 lin-lin), after an NJOY-rdelas-parity tolerance match (T/1000+5 K) for near-tabulated requests. Outside the tabulated range: hard NjoyError::TemperatureOutOfRange - silent nearest-snap is gone from parse_mf7_at_temperature. MEASURED sigma_inel(0.0253 eV, MAT 30): 500K 0.9028 b, 523.15K 0.9446 b (interpolated; strictly inside bracket), 600K 1.1108 b; selected_temperature() reports 523.15K. PREREQUISITE FIX: endf::interp::terp1 had ENDF interpolation laws 3/4 swapped (code 3 computed ln-y-linear-in-x and vice versa) vs ENDF-102 0.5.2 and upstream endf.f90; fixed with pinned unit tests, reconr/linearize midpoint arm updated. This bead can likely be closed by the maintainer after human review; P4 rationale is obsolete.

title: THERMR: S(alpha,beta) temperature interpolation (vs nearest-tabulated)

description:
Integral end-to-end validation: turbine + steam/water pipes + moisture separator reheater + condenser + feedwater as ONE self-consistent state-point set. This is the case that judges the whole secondary loop rather than a single closure.

Source: AP1000 Design Control Document, Rev. 19, Chapter 10 'Steam and Power Conversion System' (Westinghouse), NRC ADAMS accession ML11171A341, Figure 10.1-1 'rated heat balance for the turbine cycle'. Public regulatory document.

ACCESS CAVEAT: the NRC server returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching on 2026-08-04. The document and the figure were confirmed from search metadata ONLY. Download manually and verify the contents before relying on any specific number — do not cite a value that has not been read off the actual figure.

Scope context: crates/tampines-steam-tables/docs/validation-scope-turbine-and-pipe.md section 3.2.
title: V&V: secondary-cycle heat balance vs AP1000 DCD Rev.19 Fig 10.1-1

description:
Pipeline run for EBR-I. No existing bead or scoping doc — this is new.

WHY: the smallest, best-documented fast reactor to start on, and historically the one whose positive power coefficient (Mark-II core, bowing) caused the 1955 partial meltdown. That makes it an unusually good feedback-coefficient test: the sign and mechanism are published and non-obvious, so getting it right is a real check rather than a tautology.
TARGETS: criticality, then the power/temperature coefficient — specifically whether the mechanism producing it is captured, not merely the magnitude.
ENDF NEEDED: U-235, U-238 (have), Pu-239, Na-23, plus structure (all missing). No TSL needed — fast spectrum, so thermal scattering is irrelevant, which simplifies stage 1 relative to the thermal reactors.
HARDEST STAGE: feedback. Nordheim-Fuchs is in teh-o-prke and is NOT exposed to Python (confirmed missing from the wheel). Structural bowing feedback is almost certainly not modelled anywhere here — check before promising it, and if absent, say so rather than substituting a Doppler-only coefficient and calling it agreement.

Parent: op-wpi0

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: V&V information request filed as gh:#51 — what the maintainer must supply that cannot be obtained from the repo (benchmark specification and access, acceptance bands, core state, ENDF library policy, compute budget). Labelled V&V.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
SEE gh:#51 — AND A CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD. I proposed EBR-I as a validation target without checking the repo, and docs/reactor-scoping/ebr2.md section 1 already argues against it under the heading 'Why this reactor, and why not EBR-I': no modern benchmark-quality instrumented transient dataset exists; the 1955 Mark-II event rests on sparse, reconstructed 1950s data; and EBR-I used NaK, not sodium.

That reasoning is sound and my argument in this bead does not survive it — a coefficient reconstructed from sparse 1950s data cannot serve as an acceptance criterion however interesting the physics. Recommendation is to CLOSE this bead and keep EBR-II as the fast-reactor validation case. gh:#51 is tagged human-audit because 'is this evidence good enough to validate against' is a data-quality judgement for the maintainer, not for me.

title: Validate EBR-I (fast, metallic fuel, NaK)

acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified, and either a fix or a documented reconcile procedure that detects dropped records (e.g. a periodic export-vs-ref record-count/id diff).
description:
During a .beads cleanup on 2026-07-21, a record-level diff of the stale .beads/issues.jsonl.bak compat export against refs/heads/beads/store found exactly one issue present in the export but absent from the canonical store: op-hzs.14 (closed bug, 'outram-blender: uv_sphere is wound inward'). It was NOT in tombstones.jsonl, so it was not a deliberate deletion. All 335 other .bak records were a strict subset of the store.

The bead was restored by hand (bd create --id op-hzs.14, re-added the parent-child dep to op-hzs, re-closed with the original close_reason) and has since been auto-synced to origin.

Root cause unknown. Suspected window: the 2026-07-20 Go-beads to beads-rs migration, or a reconcile/merge of the store ref around 2026-07-20. Worth investigating whether the migration importer or a store merge can drop records without tombstoning them, since that would silently lose issue history.

Also note: bd's in-memory DB reported 343 issues while state.jsonl held 344 records until a bd sync forced a re-read after a fetch — possibly related, possibly a separate staleness bug.
title: beads: op-hzs.14 silently vanished from canonical beads/store ref (no tombstone)

description:
Today the best widget in the layer (281 lines, one coloured segment per FV cell, tracer marks) but geometrically inert: screen_position/screen_vector are raw screen points, PIPE_STROKE_WIDTH is a hardcoded 4.0, and there is no elevation or connection concept.

Target: stroke width from Pipe::diameter, run length from Pipe::length, angle from Pipe::inclination, endpoints shared with neighbours via the layout node graph so runs meet smoothly. All four already exist on tampines::components::Pipe -- NOT blocked on op-dt3.17.

Also: PipeScalars::mass_flow and ::residence_time are currently dead in ui() (tracer motion comes entirely from the app-owned TracerTrain) -- decide whether to use or drop them. And op-wqk.9.4 notes htgr_sim_v1 omits this widget because its fluid-array backend is too heavy to stand up; the from_scalars path exists for that, so check it actually serves the case.

Quality bar: look derives from the component's real dimensions and live state, not from arbitrary screen coordinates; document units, valid ranges and what drives what in the /// doc comment; add tests; and per the workspace V&V rule state BOTH methodology and measured results where anything is checked against a reference. Do not fabricate a value to render -- an unpopulated component must be visibly distinct from a cold one (PipeVisual's neutral-grey empty case is the precedent).
title: Widget Studio QC: PipeVisual — derive bore, run length and elevation angle from geometry
